items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: I was listening to Benny Goodman, my first hero, and trying to copy a couple of licks.

ctx.x: My dad was funny. He was in the printing business with a couple of his brothers. And once in a while he’d say, when I was listening to Benny Goodman, my first hero, and he’d go like this, “You blow that thing.” And he would forget it was a clarinet or something. But they were good. They got me a silver clarinet when I first started. I made the music class in the fourth grade. And the funny thing was they played for about 40 of us. There was a piano and the teacher said, “Okay kids. Is this the same note?” [scats]…

the Bronx, thousands of kids. And there were a couple of kids that played, they were playing sort of Benny Goodman tunes, I mean much better than me. I could barely play anything improvising. I was listening to Benny Goodman, my first hero, and trying to copy a couple of licks. I didn’t have any ear, I could play a couple of licks and I felt great. I mean three or four licks, that was it. But as a little kid you feel wonderful that you can do anything. Or play a tune, “Sing, Sing, Sing” you know. But I remember…
They stayed where they were and you got better.
